The International Planned Parenthood Federation Africa Region (IPPFAR), in collaboration with AFJCI and CRR lead the delivery of a new project called Justice for Survivors (J4S). Application Closing Date
========================

15th September 2026

Context of Role
===============

The International Planned Parenthood Federation (IPPF) is a global sexual and reproductive health (SRH) service provider and one of the leading advocates for universal access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for all. IPPF is a worldwide movement of 120 national organizations, referred to as Member Associations, working with and for communities and individuals. These member associations are the leading civil society providers of contraception in 89 of 120 countries. And in 64 of those 89 countries, IPPF is the only largescale international provider. Headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, the overarching goal of IPPF Africa Region (IPPFAR) is to increase access to SRHR services to the most vulnerable youth, men, and women in sub-Saharan Africa. To reach this goal, IPPFAR works with local civil-society organizations, governments, the African Union (AU), regional economic commissions (RECs), the United Nations, among others, to expand political and financial commitments to SRHR in Africa. IPPFAR tackles the continent's growing SRH challenges through a network of Member Associations (MAs), strategic partners and volunteers in 42 countries. For more information, please read our 20242 profile (in English and French) here.   

**Project Overview**   

**The International Planned Parenthood Federation Africa Region (IPPFAR), in collaboration with AFJCI and CRR** lead the delivery of a new project called **Justice for Survivors (J4S)** . Funded by the **Agence Francaise de Développement (AFD),** J4S's overarching goal is to strengthen the capacity of feminist movements to address gender-based violence (GBV) through sub-grants to feminist organizations, with a focus on reaching small, often unregistered, feminist organizations. The project is implemented across 4 countries: Cote d'Ivoire, Guinea, Tanzania and Kenya.   

Championing an ecological-based model that integrates the use of multi-disciplinary gender transformative approaches and direct sub-granting, J4S will provide longer-term mentorship and support to feminist organizations in their overall development, by designing specific trainings tailored to their needs and helping them identify additional sources of funding. J4S also includes a research-action component that will deepen our understanding of how these approaches can be scaled up and sustained, ensuring linking, learning, and knowledge sharing among the organizations and across regions.   

More specifically, the project seeks to:   
* Ensure and improve the sustainability of feminist organizations at the organizational and technical levels by proposing an inclusive approach to capacity strengthening.
* Reinforce the resilience and diversity of feminist civil society organizations (CSOs) through access to sustainable, flexible and adapted financing for small and/or informal and/or structurally excluded groups.
* Enhance the networking abilities of feminist CSOs from the South, bringing them closer to networks at national, regional, and international levels, in order to bring their voice to the public arena.

Role Purpose
============

* **Purpose of the Consultancy**   

The Communication Coordination Consultant will be responsible for coordinating, advising, and supporting the communication activities of the three partner organizations, ensuring alignment with the project communication strategy, branding guidelines, and donor visibility requirements.   

The consultant will not replace partners' communication teams but will provide strategic guidance, coordination, quality control, and content support to ensure consistency and effectiveness across partners.

Deliverables
============

* **Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities**   

**1. Communication Strategy and Coordination**   

* Support the development, refinement, and periodic updating of a joint project communication plan, in consultation with AFJCI, CRR, and IPPFAR.

* Ensure coherence and complementarity of communication activities across the three partners.

* Establish simple coordination mechanisms (editorial calendar, shared tools, templates) to facilitate collaboration.

* Serve as the main communication coordination focal point for the consortium.

**2. Branding, Visibility, and Quality Assurance**   

* Ensure that project branding and donor visibility guidelines are clearly understood and applied consistently by all partners.

* Review and provide feedback on key communication products produced by partners (e.g. press releases, stories, reports, visuals).

* Support partners in adapting content to different audiences while maintaining a common narrative.

**3. Content Planning and Storytelling**   

* Support partners in identifying, shaping, and prioritizing key stories, success cases, and lessons learned emerging from project activities.

* Provide guidance on messaging related to sensitive topics (e.g. gender, human rights, youth, SRHR, GBV), ensuring ethical and rights-based communication.

* **Contribute, when needed, to drafting or editing joint communication products (e.g. project highlights, case studies, donor updates).**

**4. Digital and External Communication Support**   

* Advise partners on content for websites, social media, and newsletters related to the project.

* Support coordination of joint communication moments (campaigns, international days, major project milestones).

* Ensure timely sharing of key communication outputs with all partners.

**5. Capacity Support and Knowledge Management**   

* Provide light coaching and advice to partners' communication focal points, as needed.

* Encourage systematic collection and archiving of communication materials (photos, videos, stories, testimonials).

* Support internal learning by documenting good practices and challenges in consortium communication.

**6. Reporting and Liaison**   

* Provide brief periodic updates to the project coordination team on communication progress, challenges, and upcoming priorities.

* Liaise with donor communication requirements in coordination with the lead partner.

**Deliverables (Indicative)**   

* Updates of the Project communication plan.

* Shared editorial calendar and coordination tools.

* Reviewed and harmonized key communication products across partners.

* Periodic communication briefs or highlights (frequency to be agreed).

* End-of-project communication summary and lessons learned.

**Time Allocation**   

* 2 days per week on average over the 3-year project duration.

* Level of effort may vary depending on project phases (e.g. launches, campaigns, reporting periods), with flexibility agreed in advance.

Essential Skills
================

* **Required Qualifications and Experience**   

* University degree in communications, journalism, media studies, international development, or a related field.

* At least 5 years of experience in communication roles, preferably in international development, civil society, or multi-partner projects.

* Proven experience in communication coordination and working with multiple organizations or consortia.

* Strong writing and editing skills in French or English (working knowledge of both is a strong asset).

* Demonstrated understanding of issues related to human rights, gender equality, youth, and/or SRHR.

* Experience advising on branding, donor visibility, and strategic storytelling.

**Core Competencies**   

* Strategic communication thinking

* Coordination and facilitation skills

* Excellent interpersonal and cross-cultural communication

* Ability to work independently and manage time effectively

* Attention to detail and quality assurance

* Collaborative and solution-oriented mindset

Desirable Skills
================

name: Thematic Expert - Psychosocial Support Officer (Kenya)
text: About Busara Founded in 2014, Busara is a leading behavioral science and research organization dedicated to improving development outcomes by understanding and influencing human behavior. Busara Uganda partners with governments, development agencies, foundations, research institutions, NGOs, and private sector organizations to design solutions that are evidence-based, contextually grounded, and capable of achieving impact at scale. Over the past decade, Busara has grown into one of the largest behavioral science organizations globally, combining global expertise with deep local knowledge and implementation experience. Busara's mission is to advance and apply behavioral science to help people and organizations make better decisions. The organization's distinctive value lies in its ability to connect rigorous research with practical implementation. Busara combines behavioral science, adult learning principles, human-centered design, systems thinking, and applied research methods to identify the behavioral, social, and institutional factors that influence program outcomes. This enables partners to move beyond understanding what challenges exist to understanding why they exist and how to address them sustainably. Busara supports partners across the full program lifecycle, including assessments, behavioral diagnostics, curriculum development, training and capacity strengthening, program design, monitoring and evaluation, adoption measurement, and knowledge generation. The Mastercard Foundation’s Young Africa Works Strategy aims to enable 7 million young women and men across Kenya to access dignified and fulfilling work. Through partnerships with financial institutions, training providers, enterprise support organizations, and other ecosystem actors, the initiative supports programs designed to expand employment opportunities and strengthen pathways to sustainable livelihoods for youth. Over its implementation, the scale and diversity of supported programs have grown substantially across sectors and geographies. As the strategy has matured, the Foundation’s learning priorities have shifted to place greater emphasis on understanding the nature and durability of the outcomes these programs generate. The central evidence question has shifted from assessing how many young people are reached to examining whether they can access and sustain dignified and fulfilling work as a result of these interventions. In this context, the Foundation wants to understand several interrelated dimensions of program outcomes. These include the sustainability of employment and livelihood outcomes over time, differences in outcomes across youth segments, and the extent to which interventions contribute to broader institutional and ecosystem changes. Busara is partnering with Mastercard Foundation as its Impact Partner Organization (IPO) in Kenya to conduct Program Outcomes Assessments (POA) and Strategic Reviews across Foundation-supported programs under the Young Africa Works Strategy. These assessments and reviews combine quantitative and qualitative inquiry structured around four core POA question areas, including Reach and Access, Progression to Dignified and Fulfilling Work, Improvements in Quality of Life, and Systems and Institutional Contribution, alongside program-specific objectives for each Implementing Partner reviewed. Busara is seeking the services of a Psychosocial Support Officer on a short-term basis to support work across the Young Africa Works Strategy program portfolio, whose programs incorporate gender, inclusion, and safeguarding principles into their interventions for the youth participants. Purpose of the Role The Psychosocial Support Officer will provide specialized professional expertise to safeguard participant well-being throughout the assignment, with a particular focus on identifying, preventing, and responding appropriately to emotional distress or unforeseen crises that may arise during sensitive interviews, surveys, or other field interactions. The role will also support the wider field team in maintaining a safe, ethical, and trauma-informed approach to engagement with participants \n Key Responsibilities Monitor participants for signs of distress, trauma, anxiety, or emotional overwhelm during sessions. Provide immediate emotional support and grounding techniques to help distressed participants regain a sense of safety and stability. Protect participants’ privacy by treating personal stories and mental health information with the highest level of confidentiality. Prepare data collectors to recognize and respond appropriately to emotional stress in themselves and others during the data collection exercise. Facilitate brief daily debriefs to help the team reflect on difficult experiences and support one another after demanding field days. Offer practical guidance and brief supportive counseling to staff members who may feel overwhelmed. Apply established safety protocols and ethical guidelines when engaging on sensitive topics. Escalate any significant safety concerns or incidents to lead researchers immediately. Contribute to adjustments in field plans when new emotional risks emerge during implementation. Prepare an incident report at the end of the data collection exercise, summarizing any incidents identified and the mitigation and referral measures implemented in line with Mastercard Foundation’s Safeguarding policies. Indicative Deliverables A financial proposal/quote itemizing the services to be provided. A brief psychosocial support plan outlining participant safety measures, distress response procedures, and escalation pathways for field activities. Field support notes or debrief summary capturing key wellbeing concerns, actions taken, and any follow-up needs identified during the assignment. An incident and referral log documenting any psychosocial risks, responses provided, and referrals made in line with safeguarding protocols. A concise end-of-assignment report summarizing psychosocial support activities, key observations, mitigation measures, and recommendations for future fieldwork. Required Qualifications and Experience A bachelor’s degree in social sciences, psychology, gender studies, development studies, community development, or a related field from a recognized institution in Kenya; a master’s degree is an added advantage. At least 5–7 years of professional experience in psychosocial support, safeguarding, gender-responsive programming, inclusive fieldwork, or related work in Kenya, preferably in development or humanitarian settings and with vulnerable groups such as refugees, displaced persons, women, youth, or persons with disabilities. Demonstrated experience supporting qualitative fieldwork or participant engagement, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to apply trauma-informed, culturally sensitive, and ethical approaches when working with diverse communities. Working knowledge of safeguarding principles, confidentiality, duty of care, and referral pathways in the Kenya context, including the ability to respond appropriately to sensitive disclosures. Strong communication and facilitation skills in English and Kiswahili; knowledge of additional Kenyan local languages or experience working effectively with interpreters is an advantage. Prior experience contributing to donor-funded evaluations, field research, or program reviews is an added advantage. Duration and Level of Effort Twenty (20) working days over a period of three (3) months (starting September 2026). The timelines above are indicative and will be finalized jointly with the successful consultant during the inception phase, in line with the specific review cycle for which they are engaged. \n Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications, shortlisted candidates will be notified accordingly. Data Privacy Statement As part of Busara’s recruitment process, personal information provided by an applicant through various means will be collected and stored. This includes but is not limited to the information which the candidate provides to Busara in their application and profile, any data from role assessments, interviews information including video interviews and data provided to us by your referees. This data will be used to evaluate the application, communicate with the candidate, and where a candidate has selected this option, for future recruitment opportunities. All this information will be treated as part of each job application record and only retained for the required record retention period. By choosing to apply for this position at Busara, you are giving Busara your consent to process your personal data as described above. We are committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring that your personal information is secure.

\\n

* Monitor participants for signs of distress, trauma, anxiety, or emotional overwhelm during sessions.

* Provide immediate emotional support and grounding techniques to help distressed participants regain a sense of safety and stability.

* Protect participants' privacy by treating personal stories and mental health information with the highest level of confidentiality.

* Prepare data collectors to recognize and respond appropriately to emotional stress in themselves and others during the data collection exercise.

* Facilitate brief daily debriefs to help the team reflect on difficult experiences and support one another after demanding field days.

* Offer practical guidance and brief supportive counseling to staff members who may feel overwhelmed.

* Apply established safety protocols and ethical guidelines when engaging on sensitive topics.

* Escalate any significant safety concerns or incidents to lead researchers immediately.

* Contribute to adjustments in field plans when new emotional risks emerge during implementation.

* Prepare an incident report at the end of the data collection exercise, summarizing any incidents identified and the mitigation and referral measures implemented in line with Mastercard Foundation's Safeguarding policies.

* Working knowledge of safeguarding principles, confidentiality, duty of care, and referral pathways in the Kenya context, including the ability to respond appropriately to sensitive disclosures.

* Strong communication and facilitation skills in English and Kiswahili; knowledge of additional Kenyan local languages or experience working effectively with interpreters is an advantage.

* Prior experience contributing to donor-funded evaluations, field research, or program reviews is an added advantage.

Twenty (20) working days over a period of three (3) months (starting September 2026).

Busara seeks the services of an Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development Thematic Expert on a short-term basis to support work across the Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development Portfolio, whose programs support the growth and development of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and thus provide opportunities for dignified and fulfilling work for young women and men.

Purpose of the Role

The Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development Thematic Expert brings specialist expertise in entrepreneurship, financial sector development, MSME finance, and inclusive finance mechanisms (including credit guarantees, digital financial services, and value chain finance) relevant to Kenya and the East Africa region. On this assignment, the expert leads the analysis of financial inclusion outcomes, assesses contribution to system- and ecosystem-level change in the financial sector, and contributes substantively to final review reports. The expert will support Busara and Mastercard Foundation Kenya to establish:

  • How trends in Kenya’s entrepreneurship, enterprise development, financial inclusion, and MSME sector are impacting youth employment opportunities where the strategy is active in Kenya.

  • The extent to which the strategy partnerships and investments are positioned to respond to and capitalize on these trends.

  • The barriers, gaps, and opportunities for meaningful participation of young women, persons with disabilities (PWDs), and refugee communities in entrepreneurship and enterprise development.

  • Opportunities, risks, and gaps in the strategy’s entrepreneurship, enterprise development, financial inclusion, and MSME sector positioning, and practical, prioritized recommendations to strengthen it.

\n

  • Review literature, strategy documents, partner reports, and results data on entrepreneurship, enterprise development, financial inclusion, and MSMEs in Kenya.

  • Analyze sector trends, key actors, and ecosystem dynamics, and benchmark Kenya’s context against relevant East African strategies.

  • Conduct key informant interviews and stakeholder consultations with ecosystem actors, partners, and other informed respondents.

  • Assess program relevance, coverage, and alignment with national priorities, with attention to youth employment, skilling, and participation by young women, PWDs, and refugee communities.

  • Support the design and interpretation of POA indicators, with particular attention to enterprise-based pathways and progress.

  • Assess participant experiences and outcomes related to enterprise establishment, growth, market access, productivity, resilience, financial inclusion, and business continuity.

  • Provide technical input on enterprise finance and financial inclusion pathways, including access to finance, investment decisions, loan use, repayment, and progression dynamics.

  • Support development of enterprise performance frameworks that reflect informal, emerging, and growth-oriented businesses.

  • Interpret enterprise outcomes across participant segments, including youth-owned enterprises, women-owned enterprises, refugee-owned enterprises, persons with disabilities, MSMEs, and SMEs.

  • Review quantitative and qualitative findings and synthesize evidence into actionable recommendations for program improvement, systems strengthening, and ecosystem development.

  • Review and quality-assure inception reports, analytical frameworks, interim deliverables, strategic review outputs, and final evaluation reports.

  • Produce a final report with findings, learnings, and recommendations, and a prioritization framework for Busara and Young Africa Works stakeholders.


Indicative Deliverables

  • An inception report covering the methodology, work plan, and budget.

  • Key Informant Interview (KII) discussion guides tailored to various stakeholders.

  • Audio recordings and notes from Key Informant Interview (KII) discussions.

  • A draft narrative report including an executive summary, findings, learnings and recommendations, and a prioritized action matrix.

  • A PowerPoint slide deck for presentation to the Foundation.

  • Hold a validation and dissemination session with the Foundation.

  • A final PowerPoint slide deck incorporating input from the validation and dissemination session.

  • Participate in sensemaking sessions with the Foundation, Implementing Partners, and other relevant ecosystem actors, as required.

  • A final narrative report incorporating input from the validation, dissemination, and sensemaking sessions.


Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Advanced degree in economics, finance, development studies, entrepreneurship, business administration, enterprise development, agricultural economics, private sector development, or a related field.

  • At least 8–10 years of experience in financial sector development, MSME finance, inclusive finance, enterprise development, entrepreneurship promotion, market systems development, private sector development, or livelihoods programming in Kenya or East Africa.

  • Demonstrated experience with one or more of the following: digital financial services, value chain finance, enterprise finance, or inclusive finance mechanisms.

  • Proven experience analyzing financial inclusion or enterprise development outcomes for underserved groups, including youth, women, refugees, and persons with disabilities.

  • Proven track record and consulting experience conducting strategic reviews, evaluations, or advisory assignments for donor-funded or foundation-funded entrepreneurship and enterprise development programs.

  • Strong understanding of Kenya’s financial inclusion or MSME ecosystem, including informal enterprise dynamics, growth pathways, and relevant policy and regulatory landscapes.

  • Experience working with youth entrepreneurs and inclusive enterprise development programs is highly desirable.

  • Strong analytical, report-writing, facilitation, and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to communicate technical findings to specialist and non-specialist audiences.

  • Familiarity with the Mastercard Foundation Young Africa Works strategy, Shared Measures framework, Program Outcomes Assessments (POAs), and Dignified and Fulfilling Work concepts is an advantage.


Duration and Level of Effort

Twenty-four (24) working days over a period of three (3) months (starting September 2026).

The timelines above are indicative and will be finalized jointly with the successful consultant during the inception phase, in line with the specific review cycle for which they are engaged.

Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications by August 31st 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be notified accordingly.

About Busara

Founded in 2014, Busara is a leading behavioral science and research organization dedicated to improving development outcomes by understanding and influencing human behavior. Busara Uganda partners with governments, development agencies, foundations, research institutions, NGOs, and private sector organizations to design solutions that are evidence-based, contextually grounded, and capable of achieving impact at scale. Over the past decade, Busara has grown into one of the largest behavioral science organizations globally, combining global expertise with deep local knowledge and implementation experience. Busara's mission is to advance and apply behavioral science to help people and organizations make better decisions. The organization's distinctive value lies in its ability to connect rigorous research with practical implementation. Busara combines behavioral science, adult learning principles, human-centered design, systems thinking, and applied research methods to identify the behavioral, social, and institutional factors that influence program outcomes. This enables partners to move beyond understanding what challenges exist to understanding why they exist and how to address them sustainably. Busara supports partners across the full program lifecycle, including assessments, behavioral diagnostics, curriculum development, training and capacity strengthening, program design, monitoring and evaluation, adoption measurement, and knowledge generation.

The Mastercard Foundation’s Young Africa Works Strategy aims to enable 7 million young women and men across Kenya to access dignified and fulfilling work. Through partnerships with financial institutions, training providers, enterprise support organizations, and other ecosystem actors, the initiative supports programs designed to expand employment opportunities and strengthen pathways to sustainable livelihoods for youth. Over its implementation, the scale and diversity of supported programs have grown substantially across sectors and geographies. As the strategy has matured, the Foundation’s learning priorities have shifted to place greater emphasis on understanding the nature and durability of the outcomes these programs generate. The central evidence question has shifted from assessing how many young people are reached to examining whether they can access and sustain dignified and fulfilling work as a result of these interventions. In this context, the Foundation wants to understand several interrelated dimensions of program outcomes. These include the sustainability of employment and livelihood outcomes over time, differences in outcomes across youth segments, and the extent to which interventions contribute to broader institutional and ecosystem changes.

Busara is partnering with Mastercard Foundation as its Impact Partner Organization (IPO) in Kenya to conduct Program Outcomes Assessments (POA) and Strategic Reviews across Foundation-supported programs under the Young Africa Works Strategy. These assessments and reviews combine quantitative and qualitative inquiry structured around four core POA question areas, including Reach and Access, Progression to Dignified and Fulfilling Work, Improvements in Quality of Life, and Systems and Institutional Contribution, alongside program-specific objectives for each Implementing Partner reviewed.

Busara is seeking the services of a Gender, Inclusion and Safeguarding Thematic Expert on a short-term basis to support work across the Young Africa Works Strategy program portfolio, whose programs incorporate gender, inclusion, and safeguarding principles into their interventions for the youth participants.

Purpose of the Role

The Gender, Inclusion and Safeguarding Thematic Expert brings expertise in gender-responsive evaluation, inclusive programming for structurally excluded groups, and safeguarding practice in Kenya and the East African region. On this assignment, the expert leads disaggregated analysis across gender, refugee status, and disability status; oversees qualitative data collection with these populations; ensures safeguarding standards are upheld throughout fieldwork; and ensures inclusion perspectives are reflected across all review deliverables. The expert will support Busara and Mastercard Foundation Kenya to establish:

  • How trends in Kenya’s Gender, Inclusion and Safeguarding thematic practice are impacting youth employment opportunities where the strategy is active in Kenya.

  • The extent to which the strategy’s partnerships and investments are positioned to respond to and capitalize on these trends.

  • Opportunities, risks, and gaps in the strategy’s Gender, Inclusion and Safeguarding positioning, and practical, prioritized recommendations to strengthen it.

\n


Key Responsibilities

  • Review literature, strategy documents, implementing partner reports, and results data on gender, inclusion, and safeguarding in Kenya.

  • Provide technical input to assessments and reviews related to gender, inclusion, and safeguarding ecosystem indicators.

  • Map key actors, emerging trends, and ecosystem dynamics in Kenya’s gender, inclusion, and safeguarding practice, and benchmark them against relevant East African strategies.

  • Conduct key informant interviews and stakeholder consultations with relevant actors.

  • Assess how current programs address key gender, inclusion, and safeguarding challenges, including access to services, cost barriers, and the impact of technology.

  • Assess the relevance and positioning of gender, inclusion, and safeguarding across the Young Africa Works partner portfolio and flagship interventions, including alignment with national priorities.

  • Identify barriers and opportunities for youth participation in the gender, inclusion, and safeguarding sub-sectors, to strengthen participant access to opportunities, including potential new partnerships, delivery models, priority sub-sectors, or areas of focus.

  • Evaluate the effectiveness of gender, inclusion, and safeguarding practices during youth participants' engagement, and their linkage to dignified and fulfilling work

  • Produce a report with findings, recommendations, and a prioritization framework for dissemination to Busara and the Young Africa Works stakeholders.


Indicative Deliverables

  • An inception report covering the methodology, work plan, and budget.

  • Key Informant Interview (KII) discussion guides tailored to key stakeholders.

  • Audio recordings and notes from Key Informant Interview (KII) discussions.

  • A draft narrative report including an executive summary, findings, learnings and recommendations, and a prioritized action matrix.

  • A PowerPoint slide deck for presentation to the Foundation.

  • Hold a validation and dissemination session with the Foundation.

  • A final PowerPoint slide deck incorporating input from the validation and dissemination session.

  • Participate in sensemaking sessions with the Foundation, Implementing Partners, and other relevant ecosystem actors, as required.

  • A final narrative report incorporating input from the validation, dissemination, and sensemaking sessions.


Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Advanced degree in Gender Studies, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.

  • Minimum 8-10 years of experience in gender-responsive evaluation, inclusive programming, or safeguarding in development or humanitarian contexts in Kenya, ideally including direct work with refugee or displaced populations and persons with disabilities.

  • Demonstrated experience designing and conducting qualitative fieldwork (IDIs, FGDs, KIIs) with structurally excluded groups, including trauma-informed and culturally appropriate facilitation techniques.

  • Proven track record and consulting experience conducting strategic reviews, evaluations, or advisory assignments for donor-funded or foundation-funded gender-responsive and inclusion programs.

  • Working knowledge of safeguarding frameworks and referral pathways appropriate to the Kenya context, including experience handling sensitive disclosures during fieldwork.

  • Familiarity with Kenya’s refugee response context (including major refugee settlement areas) and with national gender and disability inclusion policy is strongly preferred.

  • Strong facilitation skills in relevant Kenyan local languages, or demonstrated experience working effectively through local-language facilitators and interpreters.

  • Prior experience contributing to donor-funded evaluations or strategic reviews, ideally within mixed-methods designs, is an advantage.


Duration and Level of Effort

Twenty-four (24) working days over a period of three (3) months (starting September 2026).

The timelines above are indicative and will be finalized jointly with the successful consultant during the inception phase, in line with the specific review cycle for which they are engaged.


\n

Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications by August 31st 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be notified accordingly.


Data Privacy Statement

As part of Busara’s recruitment process, personal information provided by an applicant through various means will be collected and stored. This includes but is not limited to the information which the candidate provides to Busara in their application and profile, any data from role assessments, interviews information including video interviews and data provided to us by your referees. This data will be used to evaluate the application, communicate with the candidate, and where a candidate has selected this option, for future recruitment opportunities. All this information will be treated as part of each job application record and only retained for the required record retention period.

By choosing to apply for this position at Busara, you are giving Busara your consent to process your personal data as described above. We are committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring that your personal information is secure.

Purpose of the Role

The expert will support Busara and Mastercard Foundation Kenya to establish:

  • How digital trends (digital skilling, digital jobs and gig work, e-commerce, digital financial services, and platformisation of work) are affecting the sectors and value chains where the strategy is active.

  • The extent to which the current strategy, its partnerships, and investments are positioned to respond to and capitalize on these trends.

  • The barriers, gaps, and opportunities for meaningful participation of young women, persons with disabilities (PWDs), and refugee communities in the digital economy.

  • Conduct a literature review of Kenya’s digital economy ecosystem and review relevant Young Africa Works Strategy documents, reports, and implementing partner results data, including Kenya’s digital economy policy and regulatory context.

  • Provide technical input to the assessments and reviews relating to Digital Economy indicators, including measurement and interpretation of youth employment, inclusion, and ecosystem outcomes.

  • Map current trends in Kenya’s digital economy relevant to youth employment, such as digital skills development, online and platform-based work, e-commerce, digital financial inclusion, and county-level variation; and benchmark against relevant digital economy strategies in East Africa.

  • A final PowerPoint slide deck incorporating input from the validation and dissemination session.

  • Participate in sensemaking sessions with the Foundation, Implementing Partners, and other relevant ecosystem actors, as required.

  • A final narrative report incorporating input from the validation, dissemination, and sensemaking sessions.

  • Minimum of a Master’s degree in a relevant field such as Information Systems, ICT Policy and Regulation, Economics, Development Studies, Digital Development or Innovation, or a related field.

  • Minimum of 8-10 years’ experience working in digital economy strategy, digital inclusion, or technology-for-development, with a deep understanding of Kenya or the East African digital landscape.

  • Strong understanding of Kenya’s digital economy landscape, including digital financial services, e-commerce, gig/platform work, and relevant policy and regulatory bodies.

  • Excellent analytical, writing, and facilitation/stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information for both technical and donor/board audiences.

Twenty-four (24) working days over a period of three (3) months (starting September 2026).

The timelines above are indicative and will be finalized jointly with the successful consultant during the inception phase, in line with the specific review cycle for which they are engaged.

text: ABOUT TEAM4TECH Team4Tech ( www.team4tech.org ) envisions a world where all learners have equitable access to quality education for improved socioeconomic mobility. We advance this mission by serving as an impact accelerator for community-based education NGOs in low income communities, providing them with technical, pedagogical and operational support to help them build the durable skills their learners need for future employability. Over the past 14 years, we have supported more than 1,400 NGOs in 110 countries, improving learning opportunities and developing durable skills for 60M under-resourced learners. Team4Tech’s accelerator programming contributes to UN SDG 4 - to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. Team4Tech is building upon the technical and pedagogical foundations we have helped develop with NGOs globally to now develop their capacity to use AI to enhance their education programs. ABOUT TEAM4TECH

Team4Tech (www.team4tech.org) envisions a world where all learners have equitable access to quality education for improved socioeconomic mobility. We advance this mission by serving as an impact accelerator for community-based education NGOs in low income communities, providing them with technical, pedagogical and operational support to help them build the durable skills their learners need for future employability. Over the past 14 years, we have supported more than 1,400 NGOs in 110 countries, improving learning opportunities and developing durable skills for 60M under-resourced learners.

Team4Tech’s accelerator programming contributes to UN SDG 4 - to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. Using evidence-based practices that promote education for employability, our accelerator programming, co-designed with community-based and education-focused NGOs operating in low-resource environments, includes:

  • A robust, global online Community of Practice (CoP) to engage with free education and technology tools, workshops, certification courses, learning cohorts, and other resources;
  • Facilitated regional hubs (in Africa, South Asia, Latin America & the Caribbean, and the USA & Canada) for localized knowledge sharing and collaboration;
  • Access to skilled volunteers and educational resource partners to deliver pro bono capacity-building projects; and
  • Access to funding, amplification, and coaching to further promote NGO sustainability.

The rapid evolution of generative AI brings a new opportunity for personalized adaptive learning at scale for learners in under-resourced contexts around the world. Team4Tech is building upon the technical and pedagogical foundations we have helped develop with NGOs globally to now develop their capacity to use AI to enhance their education programs. Over the past two years, we have become the leading AI accelerator for education NGOs in low income contexts by delivering GenAI capacity building training cohorts for 80+ NGOs in more than 20 countries.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The Africa Regional Hub Lead must bring a combination of experience leading complex teams and initiatives, including direct management of senior program staff; in-depth understanding of the edtech and employment space in Africa; the ability to think strategically, link regional work to global trends, and expand Team4Tech's thought leadership on the continent; and the gravitas to represent the organization externally at high-level regional and global fora.

Specifically, the Africa Regional Hub Lead will:

Provide overall leadership of the Hub

  • Serve as the decision-maker on regional priorities, resource allocation, and program direction
  • Ensure coherence and integration across all Hub workstreams
  • Report on Hub performance, risks, and priorities to organizational leadership and the board as needed

Define and drive a cutting-edge regional strategy and translate the strategy effectively into annual workplanning

  • Develop Team4Tech’s multi-year regional strategy aligned to organizational goals and grounded in emerging trends in African edtech, employment, and workforce development
  • Translate global organizational strategy into regionally relevant priorities, and ensure regional learning informs global strategy in return
  • Define the Africa region’s annual workplan priorities based on the overall strategy and effectively utilize Team4Tech’s program management tools to ensure on-time delivery of workplan requirements

Build a cohesive, motivated, and high-performing regional team with clear expectations, responsibilities, coordination and communication structures, and deliverables

  • Directly manage all regional hub staff and contractors, providing coaching, performance feedback, and professional development support
  • Establish clear roles, workflows, meeting cadences, communication norms, and timekeeping practices across the regional team to ensure accountability and reduce duplication
  • Foster a strong team culture that supports collaboration, accountability, staff retention, and alignment with organizational values

Serve as the organization's senior representative with Ministries of Education and other key external stakeholders

  • Build and maintain high-level relationships with Ministries of Education, donors, sector networks, and private-sector partners across target countries
  • Represent Team4Tech at regional and global convenings, conferences, and policy forums
  • Support negotiations, MoUs, and partnership agreements as required for the programs in the Africa region

Ensure all programmatic activities are delivered on time, to a high standard of quality, and grounded in the evidence base

  • Oversee other regional hub team members in the execution of NGO cohort trainings, Strategic NGO and Learning Partner engagement, and program delivery milestones
  • Set and implement quality standards across program design, facilitation, and materials, in line with organizational best practices
  • Ensure program decisions and adjustments are informed by evidence and data, drawing on regional M&E findings and organizational learning

Take on a substantial leadership and management role for special funded initiatives for the Africa region, including multi-country AI capacity development programming

  • Serve as the senior accountable lead for one or more discrete, funder-specific initiatives operating alongside core Hub programming, such as multi-country AI capacity development projects that involve cascade training activities with Ministries of Education
  • Directly manage initiative-specific staff, consultants, and/or country leads, ensuring delivery against funder timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements
  • Balance this dedicated initiative leadership with the broader Hub leadership responsibilities above, prioritizing across both portfolios and flagging resourcing conflicts to organizational leadership as needed

Act as a key contributor to organizational monitoring, evaluation, and research, and feed regional priorities and learning into the M&E system

  • Champion the strategic use of M&E data for regional decision-making, funder reporting, and organizational thought leadership, in partnership with the Regional Hub Director's operational M&E oversight
  • Identify regional research and evidence-building priorities, including opportunities for rigorous evaluation in collaboration with the M&E Working Group
  • Ensure lessons learned at the regional level are captured and shared across the organization to strengthen the broader evidence base

Position the Hub as a driver of organizational and sectoral thought leadership

  • Author or contribute to publications, reports, and conference presentations that showcase regional innovations and evidence
  • Cultivate the Hub's reputation as a go-to resource on African edtech and workforce development trends among peer organizations, funders, and policymakers
  • Identify opportunities to elevate NGO partners' and staff voices in sector conversations, panels, and publications

WHO YOU ARE

A passionate advocate for Team4Tech’s mission and values. You share Team4Tech’s vision and passion to expand access to quality education and economic opportunity for under-resourced learners by leveraging technology, skilled volunteers and training resources. You thrive in an organization that believes in empowering everyone as a learner and everyone as a teacher.

AI Capacity Builder & Strategist: You possess direct experience leading AI for education initiatives in low-resource settings in Africa, AI training content development, or strategic AI advisory projects. You understand how to leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) and adaptive learning platforms to optimize pedagogical outcomes through evidence-based teaching and learning practices. Your exposure to AI has equipped you to lead thoughtful collaborations with NGOs in Africa, expanding best practices in AI implementation.

A versatile and well-rounded educator and project manager. You bring 15+ years of applicable experience in education and/or program management, ideally leading technology strategy and implementation in an educational setting. You have strong regional networks in the international development and education sectors. You also have an excellent understanding of project management techniques and methods, and you exhibit organizational, communication, and leadership skills.

A thoughtful relationship builder who develops rapport easily and fosters long-term connections. You are an ambitious go-getter, able to thrive in a fast-paced environment. You have a warm, energetic, and authentic personality that translates to building lasting relationships both internally and externally.

A well-organized and resourceful team player. You are experienced in managing multiple projects and tasks, proactively and independently addressing challenges as they arise. You have a mind for operations and efficiency, and strategically use limited resources to create systems and processes.

A professional with extensive experience supporting education NGOs and systems in Africa. You have a track record of working in diverse cultural settings and are comfortable traveling locally and regionally within Africa as well as internationally. Your exposure to international education contexts has equipped you with insights and sensitivities crucial for collaborating and communicating across cultures.

Education

  • Advanced degree (Master's or equivalent) in international education, international development, education technology, public policy, business administration, or a related field

Experience

  • 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in international development, education, or workforce development programming in sub-Saharan Africa
  • A strategic thinker who can balance big-picture vision with hands-on operational oversight
  • Demonstrated experience managing multi-country or multi-partner programs, ideally involving consortium structures (NGOs, Ministries of Education, private sector partners)
  • Experience designing and overseeing large-scale cascade or trainer-of-trainer program models in coordination with Ministries of Education
  • Experience representing an organization externally at a senior level with government counterparts, funders, and at sector convenings
  • Experience using evidence and data from M&E systems to inform organizational strategy and course corrections, ideally with exposure to designing or overseeing M&E frameworks in a multi-country context
  • Demonstrated ability to translate program data and evidence into strategic insights, funder-facing narratives, and sector-level thought leadership

Technical/functional skills

  • Strong program and people management skills, including experience building and leading a large, cohesive team across multiple countries and time zones and using technology tools for effective team management, program planning, and tracking
  • Strong familiarity with the education, technology skills, Artificial Intelligence, and/or workforce development sector in Africa; in-depth understanding of the policy and infrastructure context across the continent
  • Significant budget and grant management experience, including donor reporting and financial compliance requirements
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience contributing to thought leadership such as reports, publications, conference presentations, or similar

Relationship/networking

  • Existing network of relationships with regional stakeholders, including Ministries of Education, NGOs, donors, and/or private sector partners in the education/AI/technology space in Africa
  • Demonstrated ability to build trust and influence across diverse stakeholder groups, including government officials, funders, and grassroots implementers

Languages

  • Fluent spoken and written English required
  • French or Portuguese proficiency would be a plus

REPORTS TO

Team4Tech’s Chief Program Officer

LOCATION AND TRAVEL

This position is for a local hire in Africa (Nairobi, Kenya preferred). Team4Tech is a remote-first workplace. All roles are full-time and remote, with the expectation that the employee is willing and able to travel periodically.

The candidate is expected to travel mostly locally and regionally within Africa, approximately 30-35% of the year, for various work-related activities.

COMPENSATION

jsonLD.title: Africa Regional Hub Lead
jsonLD.description:
**ABOUT TEAM4TECH**

Team4Tech (www.team4tech.org) envisions a world where all learners have equitable access to quality education for improved socioeconomic mobility. We advance this mission by serving as an impact accelerator for community-based education NGOs in low income communities, providing them with technical, pedagogical and operational support to help them build the durable skills their learners need for future employability. Over the past 14 years, we have supported more than 1,400 NGOs in 110 countries, improving learning opportunities and developing durable skills for 60M under-resourced learners.

Team4Tech's accelerator programming contributes to UN SDG 4 - to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. Using evidence-based practices that promote education for employability, our accelerator programming, co-designed with community-based and education-focused NGOs operating in low-resource environments, includes:

* A robust, global online Community of Practice (CoP) to engage with free education and technology tools, workshops, certification courses, learning cohorts, and other resources;
* Facilitated regional hubs (in Africa, South Asia, Latin America \& the Caribbean, and the USA \& Canada) for localized knowledge sharing and collaboration;
* Access to skilled volunteers and educational resource partners to deliver pro bono capacity-building projects; and
* Access to funding, amplification, and coaching to further promote NGO sustainability.

The rapid evolution of generative AI brings a new opportunity for personalized adaptive learning at scale for learners in under-resourced contexts around the world. Team4Tech is building upon the technical and pedagogical foundations we have helped develop with NGOs globally to now develop their capacity to use AI to enhance their education programs. Over the past two years, we have become the leading AI accelerator for education NGOs in low income contexts by delivering GenAI capacity building training cohorts for 80+ NGOs in more than 20 countries.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

The Africa Regional Hub Lead must bring a combination of experience leading complex teams and initiatives, including direct management of senior program staff; in-depth understanding of the edtech and employment space in Africa; the ability to think strategically, link regional work to global trends, and expand Team4Tech's thought leadership on the continent; and the gravitas to represent the organization externally at high-level regional and global fora.

Specifically, the Africa Regional Hub Lead will:

**Provide overall leadership of the Hub**

* Serve as the decision-maker on regional priorities, resource allocation, and program direction
* Ensure coherence and integration across all Hub workstreams
* Report on Hub performance, risks, and priorities to organizational leadership and the board as needed

**Define and drive a cutting-edge regional strategy and translate the strategy effectively into annual workplanning**

* Develop Team4Tech's multi-year regional strategy aligned to organizational goals and grounded in emerging trends in African edtech, employment, and workforce development
* Translate global organizational strategy into regionally relevant priorities, and ensure regional learning informs global strategy in return
* Define the Africa region's annual workplan priorities based on the overall strategy and effectively utilize Team4Tech's program management tools to ensure on-time delivery of workplan requirements

**Build a cohesive, motivated, and high-performing regional team with clear expectations, responsibilities, coordination and communication structures, and deliverables**

* Directly manage all regional hub staff and contractors, providing coaching, performance feedback, and professional development support
* Establish clear roles, workflows, meeting cadences, communication norms, and timekeeping practices across the regional team to ensure accountability and reduce duplication
* Foster a strong team culture that supports collaboration, accountability, staff retention, and alignment with organizational values

**Serve as the organization's senior representative with Ministries of Education and other key external stakeholders**

* Build and maintain high-level relationships with Ministries of Education, donors, sector networks, and private-sector partners across target countries
* Represent Team4Tech at regional and global convenings, conferences, and policy forums
* Support negotiations, MoUs, and partnership agreements as required for the programs in the Africa region

**Ensure all programmatic activities are delivered on time, to a high standard of quality, and grounded in the evidence base**

* Oversee other regional hub team members in the execution of NGO cohort trainings, Strategic NGO and Learning Partner engagement, and program delivery milestones
* Set and implement quality standards across program design, facilitation, and materials, in line with organizational best practices
* Ensure program decisions and adjustments are informed by evidence and data, drawing on regional M\&E findings and organizational learning

**Take on a substantial leadership and management role for special funded initiatives for the Africa region, including multi-country AI capacity development programming**

* Serve as the senior accountable lead for one or more discrete, funder-specific initiatives operating alongside core Hub programming, such as multi-country AI capacity development projects that involve cascade training activities with Ministries of Education
* Directly manage initiative-specific staff, consultants, and/or country leads, ensuring delivery against funder timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements
* Balance this dedicated initiative leadership with the broader Hub leadership responsibilities above, prioritizing across both portfolios and flagging resourcing conflicts to organizational leadership as needed

**Act as a key contributor to organizational monitoring, evaluation, and research, and feed regional priorities and learning into the M\&E system**

* Champion the strategic use of M\&E data for regional decision-making, funder reporting, and organizational thought leadership, in partnership with the Regional Hub Director's operational M\&E oversight
* Identify regional research and evidence-building priorities, including opportunities for rigorous evaluation in collaboration with the M\&E Working Group
* Ensure lessons learned at the regional level are captured and shared across the organization to strengthen the broader evidence base

**Position the Hub as a driver of organizational and sectoral thought leadership**

* Author or contribute to publications, reports, and conference presentations that showcase regional innovations and evidence
* Cultivate the Hub's reputation as a go-to resource on African edtech and workforce development trends among peer organizations, funders, and policymakers
* Identify opportunities to elevate NGO partners' and staff voices in sector conversations, panels, and publications

**WHO YOU ARE**

**A passionate advocate for Team4Tech's mission and values.**You share Team4Tech's vision and passion to expand access to quality education and economic opportunity for under-resourced learners by leveraging technology, skilled volunteers and training resources. You thrive in an organization that believes in empowering everyone as a learner and everyone as a teacher.

**AI Capacity Builder \& Strategist:**You possess direct experience leading AI for education initiatives in low-resource settings in Africa, AI training content development, or strategic AI advisory projects. You understand how to leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) and adaptive learning platforms to optimize pedagogical outcomes through evidence-based teaching and learning practices. Your exposure to AI has equipped you to lead thoughtful collaborations with NGOs in Africa, expanding best practices in AI implementation.

**A versatile and well-rounded educator and project manager.** You bring 15+ years of applicable experience in education and/or program management, ideally leading technology strategy and implementation in an educational setting. You have strong regional networks in the international development and education sectors. You also have an excellent understanding of project management techniques and methods, and you exhibit organizational, communication, and leadership skills.

**A thoughtful relationship builder** who develops rapport easily and fosters long-term connections. You are an ambitious go-getter, able to thrive in a fast-paced environment. You have a warm, energetic, and authentic personality that translates to building lasting relationships both internally and externally.

**A well-organized and resourceful team player.** You are experienced in managing multiple projects and tasks, proactively and independently addressing challenges as they arise. You have a mind for operations and efficiency, and strategically use limited resources to create systems and processes.

**A professional with extensive experience supporting education NGOs and systems in Africa.** You have a track record of working in diverse cultural settings and are comfortable traveling locally and regionally within Africa as well as internationally. Your exposure to international education contexts has equipped you with insights and sensitivities crucial for collaborating and communicating across cultures.

**Education**

* Advanced degree (Master's or equivalent) in international education, international development, education technology, public policy, business administration, or a related field

**Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in international development, education, or workforce development programming in sub-Saharan Africa
* A strategic thinker who can balance big-picture vision with hands-on operational oversight
* Demonstrated experience managing multi-country or multi-partner programs, ideally involving consortium structures (NGOs, Ministries of Education, private sector partners)
* Experience designing and overseeing large-scale cascade or trainer-of-trainer program models in coordination with Ministries of Education
* Experience representing an organization externally at a senior level with government counterparts, funders, and at sector convenings
* Experience using evidence and data from M\&E systems to inform organizational strategy and course corrections, ideally with exposure to designing or overseeing M\&E frameworks in a multi-country context
* Demonstrated ability to translate program data and evidence into strategic insights, funder-facing narratives, and sector-level thought leadership

**Technical/functional skills**

* Strong program and people management skills, including experience building and leading a large, cohesive team across multiple countries and time zones and using technology tools for effective team management, program planning, and tracking
* Strong familiarity with the education, technology skills, Artificial Intelligence, and/or workforce development sector in Africa; in-depth understanding of the policy and infrastructure context across the continent
* Significant budget and grant management experience, including donor reporting and financial compliance requirements
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience contributing to thought leadership such as reports, publications, conference presentations, or similar

**Relationship/networking**

* Existing network of relationships with regional stakeholders, including Ministries of Education, NGOs, donors, and/or private sector partners in the education/AI/technology space in Africa
* Demonstrated ability to build trust and influence across diverse stakeholder groups, including government officials, funders, and grassroots implementers

**Languages**

* Fluent spoken and written English required
* French or Portuguese proficiency would be a plus

**REPORTS TO**

Team4Tech's Chief Program Officer

**LOCATION AND TRAVEL**

This position is for a local hire in Africa (Nairobi, Kenya preferred). Team4Tech is a remote-first workplace. All roles are full-time and remote, with the expectation that the employee is willing and able to travel periodically.

The candidate is expected to travel mostly locally and regionally within Africa, approximately 30-35% of the year, for various work-related activities.

**COMPENSATION**

Salary is commensurate with experience and geographic location, ranging from KES 650,000-800,000 monthly. Standard benefits package for Kenya based employees include health insurance, paid time off, pension, etc.

**TO APPLY**

Please submit your application through our Breezy HR portal. Only applications submitted through our Breezy HR portal will be considered at this time.

Applications will be considered on a rolling basis and handled with confidentiality. Preference will be given to applications received by September 18th, 2026. Desired start date in November 2026.

Plant Operations and Equipment Maintenance

  • Operate, monitor, and maintain plant machinery and equipment in accordance with operating procedures and manufacturer specifications.
  • Conduct routine inspections of machinery, equipment, electrical/mechanical systems, and other plant installations.
  • Perform preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance activities.
  • Identify equipment defects, abnormalities, leaks, unusual noises, vibrations, overheating, and other potential faults.
  • Carry out repairs and replacements of worn or defective components.
  • Ensure machinery is properly lubricated, adjusted, calibrated, and maintained.
  • Assist with installation, commissioning, modification, and decommissioning of plant equipment.
  • Ensure plant equipment is maintained in a condition that supports continuous and efficient production.

Fault Finding and Troubleshooting

  • Diagnose mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and other equipment-related faults.
  • Respond promptly to equipment breakdowns and emergencies.
  • Undertake corrective actions to restore equipment to operational condition.
  • Escalate complex technical problems to the Maintenance/Plant Manager or relevant specialist.
  • Conduct root-cause analysis for recurring equipment failures and recommend corrective measures.
  • Maintain accurate records of breakdowns, repairs, and equipment performance.

Preventive Maintenance

  • Implement scheduled preventive maintenance activities in accordance with the plant maintenance plan.
  • Inspect critical equipment and identify potential failures before they result in breakdowns.
  • Maintain maintenance checklists and ensure scheduled tasks are completed within the required timelines.
  • Recommend replacement or refurbishment of equipment and components where necessary.
  • Support the development and improvement of preventive maintenance schedules.

Safety and Compliance

  • Comply with all occupational health and safety requirements, company policies, and plant procedures.
  • Follow safe work procedures when working on machinery, electrical systems, moving equipment, and other hazardous plant installations.
  • Apply Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures before undertaking maintenance or repair work where applicable.
  • Properly use Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
  • Immediately report unsafe conditions, equipment hazards, incidents, near misses, and environmental risks.
  • Participate in safety inspections, toolbox talks, emergency drills, and risk assessments.
  • Ensure maintenance activities do not compromise the safety of employees, contractors, visitors, or plant operations.

Production Support

  • Work closely with production teams to ensure equipment availability and minimize production interruptions.
  • Provide technical support during equipment start-up, shutdown, changeovers, and production activities.
  • Respond to production-related equipment concerns and technical requests.
  • Advise operators on correct equipment operation and basic maintenance requirements.
  • Support efforts to improve equipment reliability, productivity, and efficiency.

Spare Parts and Tools

  • Identify and communicate requirements for spare parts, consumables, tools, and maintenance materials.
  • Ensure tools and equipment are properly maintained, stored, and accounted for.
  • Assist in maintaining appropriate stock levels of critical spare parts.
  • Verify that replacement components meet required technical specifications.
  • Minimize wastage and ensure responsible use of maintenance materials.

Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate maintenance records, equipment history, inspection reports, and breakdown reports.
  • Complete maintenance work orders and job cards accurately and on time.
  • Record equipment readings, maintenance activities, faults, repairs, and replacement parts.
  • Prepare reports on equipment performance, downtime, recurring faults, and maintenance activities as required.
  • Ensure maintenance documentation is properly filed and readily available for reference and audits.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve plant reliability, efficiency, safety, and productivity.
  • Participate in root-cause analysis and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Recommend modifications or improvements to machinery and plant systems.
  • Support initiatives aimed at reducing equipment downtime, maintenance costs, energy consumption, and production losses.
  • Keep up to date with relevant technical developments, equipment technologies, and maintenance practices.

Housekeeping and Environmental Responsibilities

  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe maintenance work area.
  • Ensure tools, equipment, and spare parts are stored appropriately after use.
  • Dispose of used oils, lubricants, damaged components, and other maintenance waste in accordance with environmental requirements.
  • Prevent and promptly report oil, chemical, fuel, or other hazardous-material spills.
  • Support the plant's environmental management and sustainability initiatives.

Requirements

  • Minimum tertiary qualification - Diploma or Degree in Mechanical/Electrical Electromechanical, Mechatronics, or Industrial Engineering, or in a relevant field.
  • Trade Test certification.
  • PLC/Automation certification.
  • Certification / Knowledge of warehouse machinery, refrigeration systems, or facility equipment.
  • Office clerical procedures.
  • 3-5 years' experience in an automated manufacturing, processing, FMCG, cold-chain, or industrial environment with experience operating and maintaining production equipment – Avoline etc.
  • Attention to detail
  • Able to work under pressure and independently
  • Time management
  • Assertive, organized and proactive
  • Leadership Skills
  • Delivers high output and is deadline driven
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
  • Knowledge of PLC-controlled equipment.
  • Understanding of sensors, actuators, VFDs, and control panels.

name: Human Resource Officer
text: Job Title: Human Resource Officer Location: Nairobi Position Overview: In your role as a HRO based in Nairobi, your main duty is to supervise all HR and administrative tasks encompassing recruitment, contracting, onboarding, performance management, attendance, disciplinary matters, and offboarding for personnel at our client site. Furthermore, you will play a pivotal role in fostering and maintaining robust work place relationships. Key Responsibilities 1. Leave Management: Efficiently manage leave requests for direct staff members. 2. Employee Onboarding: Facilitate a seamless onboarding process for new hires, ensuring timely issuance of contracts. 3. Employee Relations: Act as a key point of contact for addressing employee concerns or grievances, fostering a positive work environment. 4. Performance Management: Support the performance evaluation process for direct staff members. 5. HR Data Management: Maintain accurate HR records and data, including employee files, attendance records, and training documentation. 6. Payroll Processing: Ensure accurate processing of payroll for all employees, including verification of timesheets, salary adjustments, and deductions. 7. Compliance and Legal Requirements: Stay abreast of changes in labor laws and ensure compliance with employment regulations and internal policies. 8. Client Retention and Growth: Drive retention and growth of the existing customer base through exceptional service delivery and maintaining strong client relationships. Requirements Qualifications and Skills • Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience as a HR practitioner or in an operations role in a dynamic business environment. • Bachelor's degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, or a related field from a reputable institution. A Master's degree is an added advantage. • Strong organizational and time management skills. • Proficiency in Google Suite, Microsoft Office, and HRMIS systems. • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. • Ability to troubleshoot and resolve operational challenges efficiently. Preferred: • Understanding of Kenya's Employment Laws. • Proven ability to take ownership, deliver results, foster team success, and drive change. • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills. • Strong people management and attention to detail capabilities. • Ability to work effectively with a diverse group of individuals

name: Sales Representative (Interior Design)
text: Job Summary We’re looking for a dynamic Sales Representative with a strong foundation in interior design to lead client engagement. This role bridges design sensibility with strategic sales, ensuring every client receives tailored solutions that elevate their spaces. Key Responsibilities • Drive sales of custom furniture solutions by understanding client needs and translating them into design-forward proposals. • Lead consultations with residential and commercial clients, providing expert guidance on furniture styles, finishes, and layout. • Collaborate closely with design and production teams to ensure feasibility and timely delivery of orders. • Develop and execute sales strategies to grow revenue and expand market reach. • Build and maintain long-term client relationships through exceptional service and consistent follow- up. • Track sales performance, prepare reports, and present insights and recommendations to leadership. • Represent the brand at trade shows, design expos, and client events. Requirements Requirements & Qualifications • Bachelor’s degree in Interior Design; sales experience is an added advantage. • 3–5 years’ proven experience in sales, preferably in furniture, interior design, or luxury goods. • Strong understanding of design principles, space planning, and material selection. • Excellent communication and presentation skills. • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, CRM tools, and design software (e.g.,Canva, SketchUp, or similar). • Ability to manage multiple projects and client expectations simultaneously. • Passion for design, craftsmanship, and customer satisfaction. What We Offer • Competitive salary with performance-based incentives. • Opportunities for professional growth and creative collaboration. • A vibrant, design-focused work environment. • Employee discounts on custom furniture. • Access to industry events and training.

name: Project Manager-Oracle E Business Suite (Re-implementation)
text: Role Classification: Project Management Employment Type: Contract- Fixed term project based Program Duration : 21 months Job Purpose The Project Manager will lead the end-to-end re-implementation of Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) and associated Oracle applications across Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Projects, Warehouse Management, and Human Resources functions. The role will be responsible for delivering the ERP transformation program on time, within budget, and to the agreed quality standards while ensuring alignment with business objectives and operational requirements. Scope of the Oracle EBS re-implementation The Project Manager will lead the re-implementation and integration of the following Oracle modules: Financial Management • Oracle Payables • Oracle Receivables • Oracle Cash Management • Oracle General Ledger • Oracle Fixed Assets • Oracle Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) Supply Chain & Procurement • Oracle Inventory • Oracle Purchasing • Oracle iProcurement • Oracle Warehouse Management • Oracle Spares Management Manufacturing & Planning • Material Requirements Planning (MRP) • Oracle Process Manufacturing (OPM) • Oracle Process Manufacturing Process Planning • Oracle Process Manufacturing Process Execution • Oracle Process Manufacturing Quality Management Order Fulfillment • Order Management Human Capital Management • Oracle Core HRMS Project Management • Oracle Projects Key Responsibilities • Provide overall program leadership and governance. • Manage scope, schedule, budget, risks, issues, and resources. • Coordinate business stakeholders, implementation partners, and technical teams. • Lead business process transformation, testing, change management, and training. • Oversee data migration, integrations, cutover, and go-live activities. • Report progress to executives and steering committees. Requirements Required Qualifications • Bachelor’s Degree in IT, Business, Finance, Engineering, or related fields. • MBA preferred. • PMP, PRINCE2, Agile or equivalent. • Oracle certification. Experience Requirements • 5+ years of project management experience including leading Oracle ERP/EBS implementations in the manufacturing industry. • Experience across Finance, Procurement, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Warehouse, and HR functions. Core Competencies • Leadership • Stakeholder Management • Vendor Management • Change Management • Risk Management • Financial Acumen • Communication and Negotiation
